nodes.description: Besides IRF6, RIPK4 phosphorylates other substrates. It phosphorylates the Wnt adaptor DVL2 to promote canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, and Bartsocas-Papas RIPK4 mutants fail to induce beta-catenin accumulation. It also phosphorylates LATS1/2 in liquid condensates, acting as an upstream kinase of a noncanonical Hippo pathway; in Ripk4 knockout epidermis Yap/Taz are activated in the granular layer and repress cholesterol biosynthesis, and removing Yap/Taz partly rescues the barrier defect. Disease-derived RIPK4 mutants fail to activate LATS1/2. How much these branches contribute to the human malformations is not known.

nodes.description: RIPK4 sits in a transcriptional and signaling axis of the surface ectoderm. p63, the master regulator of stratified epithelia, directly activates RIPK4 transcription, and IRF6 also controls RIPK4 expression. RIPK4 phosphorylates IRF6 at Ser413 and Ser424, priming IRF6 for activation and nuclear entry, where it induces differentiation regulators such as GRHL3 and OVOL1. The role of RIPK4 in mouse development requires its kinase activity. Loss of RIPK4 kinase activity therefore weakens the IRF6-dependent differentiation program, which is why the RIPK4 and IRF6 pterygium syndromes resemble each other.

nodes.description: The periderm is a transient superficial epithelial layer that forms early in embryogenesis and keeps apposed, adhesion-competent embryonic epithelia from sticking together. In Ripk4-deficient mice periderm development is abnormal, E-cadherin is mislocalized to the apical membrane of the outer peridermal cells, and all external orifices fuse; deleting E-cadherin in keratinocytes rescues the oral and tail-to-body fusions. Failure of periderm formation is the proposed common mechanism of the popliteal pterygium, cocoon and Bartsocas-Papas syndromes. In patients this produces the popliteal and other pterygia, ankyloblepharon, the fibrous bands between the jaws and the fused lips.

evidence.snippet: a homozygous one base-pair insertion mutation (c.777_778insA) predicted to lead to a premature stop codon (p.Arg260ThrfsX14) within the kinase domain
